newsitem.title: USA: US West Coast gasolines up on production concerns.
newsitem.headline: US West Coast gasolines up on production concerns.

text.p: U.S. West Coast gasoline prices extended yesterday's strong gains Friday, amid moderate trade and concerns about production shortages from regional refineries, traders said.
The union representing Unocal's refinery workers said Friday a possible strike would not happen until late Monday.
Traders worried a major source of California gasoline production would be lost. The four Unocal refineries process 250,000 barrels-per-day (bpd) of crude and make 20 percent of California's gasoline.
The strike threat follows the union's rejection last week of a contract offer from Tosco Corp, which takes over the facilities next month.
Gasoline also found strength because of prolonged maintenance at Exxon, Mobil, and Unocal plants, which are expected to return next week.
"Product is tight. There's been rumors of majors buying," one broker said.
Bids for conventional unleaded gasoline in Los Angeles rose two cents to 80 cents a gallon, while buyers valued CARB-grade material one cent higher at 82 cents.
Offers for San Francisco conventional rose three cents to 81 cents.
